name: find_sounds
description: Find sounds on this computer by words in their file and folder names ("kick", "808", "vinyl"), or pick some at random. Searches the folders the producer names, as full paths or ~/…, and otherwise where Live keeps samples: the User Library, Live's Core Library and Factory Packs. Returns each sample's name, path and length in seconds (for WAV and AIFF).

folders.description: Folders to search, such as ~/Samples; Live's User Library when empty

words.description: Every word must appear in the file's name or its folders

random.description: Pick at random among the matches instead of the best ones

limit.description: How many to return (20 when unset)

name: read_notes
description: Read MIDI clips' notes in Kumi's notation (the same you write): bar|beat positions, in song time for Arrangement clips and the clip's own time and meter for Session clips; drums on a Drum Rack come as lanes. Each clip says whether the text holds all of the notes (exact). format "json" gives Live's own note rows instead, for edits by note id.

clipRef.description: A MIDI clip from this turn (Session or Arrangement)

name: make_device
description: Make a Max for Live device the producer asks for: a MIDI effect, an audio effect or an instrument. Kumi writes it to their User Library for load_device. Read the guide for the kind first (guide: true, type): how to patch it, where code belongs, the rules Kumi checks, and what makes a device good. To learn Max's objects (what each is for, its arguments, its inlets and outlets for the arguments given, its messages and attributes), give objects: ["pipe", "makenote 60 100 250"]: Kumi answers from this machine's Max, faster than the web and right for the Max the device runs in, and makes nothing. Then give its type, name, what it does, its controls (knobs, menus, switches and triggers, which become ordinary Live parameters, each in its group) and its patch: Max's own objects in Kumi's notation, with code only in the boxes that need it (GenExpr in [gen~], JavaScript in [v8] and [v8ui]). A device that's one box of code can be given as code instead: JavaScript for a MIDI effect, with tests Kumi runs; GenExpr for an audio effect, or for one voice of an instrument, which Kumi plays as many voices. Kumi builds the device around the patch or the code, lays its face out in Live's own style, keeps what plays in time on Live's grid with its building blocks ([kumi.clock], [kumi.notes], [kumi.transport]), gives a device that modulates a Map page of slots, checks it and always makes it: what's wrong comes back beside it, by line, with what Kumi changed to make it, and making it again in this conversation with the same name replaces it. Build what the producer asks for, as fully as they ask: as many controls as it needs, and the original's behaviour when recreating one. Kumi's rules keep a device safe and loadable; they don't limit its scope, and its ceilings are generous. Then load it with load_device and the itemId it returns, and hear an audio effect or instrument with audition.

guide.description: true: read how to make a device of this type (first)

objects.description: Max objects to learn, each as it's typed in a box ("makenote 60 100 250"): Kumi answers from this machine's Max and makes nothing

type.description: midi_effect, audio_effect or instrument; midi_effect when left out

name.description: The device's name, as the producer would say it

about.description: What it does, in a sentence or two

default.description: A number, one of the options, or true/false

group.description: The section of the face it's in, under this heading (controls that work together)

show.description: How it shows: a number as a dial (default), number box or slider; a choice as a menu (default) or tabs

patch.description: The device as a patch of Max's own objects in Kumi's notation, with code in [gen~], [v8] and [v8ui] boxes where objects do the job badly, and Kumi's building blocks for what plays in time (see the guide)

map.description: A patch that sends modulation to mod (0 to 1) gets a Map page: its slots (8 when left out) and its sources' names (mod.0, mod.1…)

code.description: Instead of patch, for a device that's one box of code: a MIDI effect's JavaScript (function midi(event) and helpers, with tests), or an audio effect's or one instrument voice's GenExpr (see the guide)

voices.description: An instrument's voices: how many notes play at once, 1 for mono (8 when left out)

runs_free.description: A MIDI effect that keeps sending on its own once every note is released (an LFO, a clock, a generator)

items.description: { type: noteon|noteoff|cc|pitchbend|aftertouch|polytouch|program, pitch, velocity, controller, value, channel, at (ms) }
{ type: noteon|noteoff|cc|pitchbend|aftertouch|polytouch|program, pitch, velocity, controller, value, channel, at (ms) }

name: set_tempo
description: Change the Set's tempo in BPM (20–999).

name: set_mixer
description: Change one track's mixer. volume is the fader position from 0 to 1 (0.85 is 0 dB, 1 is +6 dB); pan goes from -1 (left) to 1 (right); mute and solo are on/off; sends are levels from 0 to 1 for return tracks A, B, … in order (a shorter list leaves the rest). trackRef comes from discovery in this turn; return tracks and the main track work too.

name: rename
description: Rename a track, scene, clip, device or locator. kind says which; ref comes from discovery in this turn.

name: add_tracks_and_scenes
description: Add new MIDI or audio tracks and named scenes. New ones go after the last track or scene unless you give an index (0 is first). References from earlier in this answer still name the same tracks and scenes afterwards; the answer says when they don't.

name: write_midi_clip
description: Write a new MIDI clip into an empty Session slot. trackRef is a MIDI track from discovery in this turn; sceneIndex 0 is the first scene; length and every note's start and duration are in beats from the clip start (a 4/4 bar is 4 beats); pitch 60 is middle C (C3 in Live); velocity is 1–127. Or give notation (Kumi's notation, in the clip's own bars) instead of notes, and leave length out to take whole bars.

name: load_sample
description: Load a sample into a new Simpler on an empty MIDI track (add the track first): one change, undone as one. sample is the path of an audio file (one find_sounds returned, or any on this computer); trackRef comes from discovery in this turn or the track just added.

sample.description: The path of an audio file (one find_sounds returned, or any on this computer), or {"random": true, "words": ["kick"]} for Kumi to pick one itself (words and folders optional)

name: load_sample_to_pad
description: Load a sample onto an empty pad of a Drum Rack, in a new Simpler on that pad, or in Live 12's Drum Sampler with instrument "Drum Sampler"; undo clears the pad. deviceRef is the Drum Rack from discovery in this turn; note is the pad's note: 36 (C1) is the first pad, then 37, 38 and so on up to 51 on a new rack. sample is the path of an audio file (one find_sounds returned, or any on this computer).

note.description: The pad: 36 is C1, the first pad

sample.description: The path of an audio file (one find_sounds returned, or any on this computer), or {"random": true, "words": ["kick"]} for Kumi to pick one itself (words and folders optional)

instrument.description: Simpler unless the producer asks for Drum Sampler

name: load_device
description: Load an instrument, effect, Max for Live device or preset from Live's Browser onto a track (after its devices) or, with chainRef instead, into a rack's chain (after the chain's devices; a chain can hold a rack too). itemId is the Browser path, such as "instruments/Drum Rack", "instruments/Operator", "audio_effects/Reverb" or a modulator, "modulators/LFO" (and Shaper, Envelope Follower, Expression Control); live_browser_search finds others. A track or a chain takes one instrument: to layer instruments, load an Instrument Rack, add a chain for each with edit_rack, and load one into each. trackRef and chainRef come from discovery in this turn or an earlier step.

name: set_device_parameter
description: Set one device parameter to a value between its min and max, or several of one device at once with values (one change, one undo) when offered. deviceRef and parameterRef come from discovery in this turn; instead of parameterRef, parameter names it ("Drive"), found on the device when the step runs: that's how a plan or a recipe sets a device an earlier step loaded (deviceRef "@sat").

parameter.description: The parameter's name on the device, as Live shows it; instead of parameterRef

name: edit_rack
description: Work on a rack (instrument, audio effect, MIDI effect or drum rack): add-chain (chains play side by side, in parallel; mark it with as and load devices into it with load_device's chainRef; index 0 is first), add-macro or remove-macro, randomize-macros (Live's Rand button), store-variation (the macros' current settings, as a new variation), recall-variation or delete-variation (index), select-variation (index), or copy-pad (a drum rack's pad sourceIndex to targetIndex, notes 0–127). rackRef is the rack from discovery in this turn or an earlier step. Macro values are the rack's "Macro 1", "Macro 2", … parameters: set them with set_device_parameter.

index.description: add-chain: where the chain goes, 0 is first (left out, after the last); variations: which one, 0 is first

name: set_chain_mixer
description: Balance a rack's chains: one chain's volume (0 to 1; 0.85 is 0 dB), pan (-1 left to 1 right), or chainActivator false to switch the chain off (true on). chainRef comes from discovery in this turn or an earlier step.

name: set_locators
description: Mark a section in the Arrangement with two named locators. start and end are in beats from the start of the song (bar 1 is beat 0; a 4/4 bar is 4 beats).

name: set_track_color
description: Change a track's colour to one of Live's 70 palette colours (colorIndex 0–69). ref comes from discovery in this turn.

name: set_transport
description: Change the transport: the loop (loopEnabled, loopStart and loopLength in beats; a 4/4 bar is 4 beats), the metronome, punch in and out, and the playhead position (beats). Playing and stopping are the play tool's.

name: set_routing
description: Route a track and get it ready to record: its input (inputType and inputSubRouting, such as another track and "Post FX", or "Resampling" for the main output; never "Main", which crashes Live) and output (outputType, outputSubRouting), exactly as Live names them (live_discover kind routing-choice with the track as parent lists them), arm on or off, and monitoring in, auto or off. A new audio track fed by another track and armed is how audio gets bounced (resampling).

name: set_mixer_options
description: A track's other mixer settings: trackActivator (the track on or off), crossfadeAssign (0 none, 1 A, 2 B), panningMode (0 stereo, 1 split) with panningLeft and panningRight (-1 to 1), and the main track's crossfader (-1 A to 1 B).

name: edit_rack_mapping
description: Experimental Willington rack edits: kind macro-name renames macroIndex 0–15; variation-name renames the selected variation; macro-mapping assigns targetRef to mappingIndex 0–15 with minimum, maximum and mappingKind continuous, enum or boolean. Null mappingIndex unmaps. Boolean endpoints are macro thresholds 0–127; others use target parameter units. Kinds key-zone, velocity-zone and selector-zone edit one regular chain: ref is its parent rack, targetRef the chain; minimum, maximum, fadeMinimum and fadeMaximum are integer endpoints. Omitted endpoints retain their current values; supply an ordered complete range, with velocity 1–127 and key/selector 0–127. Audio Effect Racks support selector zones only; Instrument and MIDI Effect Racks support all three. Requires stopped playback.

name: set_clip_follow_actions
description: Set Session clip Follow Actions with experimental Willington support. Requires stopped playback. Actions: 0 none, 1 stop, 2 again, 3 previous, 4 next, 5 first, 6 last, 7 any, 8 other, 9 jump. Chances are percentages; supplying one sets the complementary chance. Linked timing uses loop count; unlinked time uses beats. Jump targets are 1-based scene numbers. For launch Legato, use set_clip with legato: true after creating the clip. Does not change scene Follow Actions or the global switch.

name: set_clip
description: Change a clip's settings: muted, colorIndex (0–69), looping with loopStart and loopEnd (beats from the clip's start), launchMode (0 trigger, 1 gate, 2 toggle, 3 repeat), launchQuantization (0 global, then none, 8 bars, 4, 2, 1 bar, 1/2, 1/2T, 1/4, 1/4T, 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16, 1/16T, 1/32), legato, ramMode and velocityAmount (0–1). clipRef comes from discovery (a clip-slot's clipRef).

name: set_audio_clip
description: Change an audio clip: gain (Live's clip gain control, 0–1; discover the clip first and move from its current value), pitchCoarse (semitones, ±48) and pitchFine (cents, ±50), loopStart and loopEnd, warping on or off and warpMode (0 Beats, 1 Tones, 2 Texture, 3 Re-Pitch, 4 Complex, 6 Complex Pro). Live's API has no clip fades. clipRef comes from discovery.

name: edit_clip
description: Edit a clip's content: crop (to its loop), duplicate-loop (doubles the loop, content and all), duplicate-region (copies regionStart–regionEnd to destination, in beats), or move-playing-position (by offset beats). Live gives Kumi no undo for these (Live's own undo can).

name: duplicate_clip
description: Copy a clip: into a Session slot (targetTrackRef and targetSceneIndex, 0 is the first scene; the same track when targetTrackRef is left out) or into the Arrangement at arrangementPosition (beats; a 4/4 bar is 4 beats). This is also how MIDI reaches the Arrangement: write the clip in Session view, then duplicate it there.

name: move_clip
description: Move a clip: an Arrangement clip to a new position (beats), on its own track or another of its kind (targetTrackRef), replacing what's there as dropping it in Live does (the preview names it; Kumi's undo brings it back, except after a copy or a move to another track, which Live's own undo takes back, and never per-note expression or follow actions, which Live doesn't give Kumi); keepSource: true copies it there instead, leaving it where it is. Or a Session clip to another slot (targetTrackRef and targetSceneIndex, both needed; the clip's own track to keep it on its track).

name: add_arrangement_clip
description: Put a clip in the Arrangement at position (beats from the Set's start): an empty MIDI clip (trackRef, a MIDI track; length in beats; a name), or an audio file as a clip (sample, its path, as find_sounds gives it; trackRef, an audio track). For a MIDI clip with notes, write_arrangement_clip writes them in one go.

takeLaneRef.description: A take lane on the track (add_take_lane gives one), for a MIDI clip in it: the clip needs a name, and a span no clip in the lane is in (Live's API can't put back a lane clip it cuts)

sample.description: An audio file's path, for an audio clip

name: add_take_lane
description: Add a take lane to a track in the Arrangement (Live's lanes for takes and comping): trackRef, and a name if you like. Put a MIDI clip in it with add_arrangement_clip's takeLaneRef, or an audio file with import_audio's. Live's API can't delete a take lane; Live's own undo takes it back.

name: change_notes
description: Change notes already in a clip, Session or Arrangement, by id: pitch, start, duration (beats), velocity, mute, probability, velocityDeviation, releaseVelocity. Get their ids first: read_notes with format json lists a clip's notes with their ids, and live_note_read with selected: true gives the ones selected in Live. start is in the clip's own time, an Arrangement clip's too (read_notes' json gives it so; its placement says where the clip plays).

name: delete_notes
description: Delete notes from a clip, Session or Arrangement, by id (read_notes with format json lists them with their ids).

name: edit_notes
description: Quantize a clip's notes (Session or Arrangement) (action quantize: grid in beats, 0.25 is 1/16; amount 0–1), move them to one pitch (quantize-pitch with pitch), or duplicate them (duplicate). noteIds limits it to some notes; left out, all. select selects notes in the clip as a click would (noteIds, all: true or none: true; nothing to undo); delete-range deletes the notes starting in a region of pitch (fromPitch, pitchSpan) and time (fromTime, timeSpan, in beats of the clip's own time, as read_notes' json gives notes).

name: transform_midi
description: Transform or generate a clip's notes (Session or Arrangement). transform and its params: transpose {semitones}; scale-constrain {root 0–11 (0 is C), scale}; quantize {grid beats, amount, target start|end|both}; swing {grid, amount}; velocity-curve {curve linear-up|linear-down|arch|exp-up|exp-down, amount}; humanize-velocity {maxDelta}; humanize-timing {maxOffset beats}; legato {gap}; staccato {factor 0.05–1}; rotate {steps} (rotates pitches, keeps rhythm); repeat {times 2–8, decay}; ratchet {subdivisions 2–16, probability}; chord-voicing {strategy close|open|drop2}; arpeggiate {pattern up|down|updown|downup|random, rate beats}; seeded-variation {velocityMax, timingMax, probabilityDepth, seed}; euclidean {pulses, steps, rotation, pitch, velocity, stepLength, noteLength, bars}; chord-progression {chords ["Cm","Ab","Eb","Bb"] or roman numerals with root and scale, voicing close|drop2|spread, chordDuration beats, octave, velocity}; drum-pattern {style four-on-the-floor|backbeat|breakbeat|trap-hats, bars, density 0–1, mapping {kick: 36, snare: 38, closedHat: 42, …}}; bassline {pattern octave|walking|arpeggiated, chords, root, scale, stepBeats, octave}; motif-invert {axis pitch}; motif-retrograde {}; motif-augment and motif-diminish {numerator, denominator}. Scales: major, minor, harmonic-minor, melodic-minor, dorian, phrygian, lydian, mixolydian, locrian, major-pentatonic, minor-pentatonic, blues, chromatic. scope duplicate writes the result to a copy in a Session slot (target {trackRef, sceneIndex}) and leaves the original; generative ones (repeat, ratchet, arpeggiate, euclidean, chord-progression, drum-pattern, bassline) do by default. An Arrangement clip's notes change in place, so the generative ones need a Session clip.

name: set_automation
description: Draw automation inside a Session clip for one device parameter: create-envelope, then insert points ({time in beats from the clip start, value in the parameter's own range}), insert-step (start and length in beats, value: one value held for that long; it makes the lane when there's none), delete-range (from, to), or delete-envelope. clipRef from discovery; parameterRef from discovering the device's parameters. The Arrangement's automation lanes aren't reachable.

name: change_structure
description: Add a return track (create-return, with a name), delete one (delete-return, ref; Live gives Kumi no undo for this), or duplicate a track or scene (duplicate-track, duplicate-scene, ref). References from earlier in this answer still name the same tracks and scenes afterwards, except sends once a return is deleted; the answer says when they don't.

name: set_scene
description: Change a scene: colorIndex (0–69), its own tempo (tempo with tempoEnabled) and time signature (signatureNumerator, signatureDenominator with timeSignatureEnabled), which Live switches to when the scene launches. ref is the scene from discovery.

name: capture_scene
description: Capture the clips playing now into a new scene (Live's Capture and Insert Scene).

name: switch_device
description: Switch a device on or off (its Device On button): deviceRef from discovery, enabled true or false.

name: move_device
description: Move a device along its own track's chain: deviceRef, and index (0 is first; -1 is last). To another track or into a rack's chain, use move_device_to.

name: move_device_to
description: Move a device to another track (targetTrackRef) or into a rack's chain (targetChainRef), at index (0 is first).

name: delete_device
description: Delete a device (ref from discovery). Kumi can't bring it back (Live's own undo can).

name: set_chain
description: Change a rack chain: mute, solo, colorIndex (0–69) or autoColor. chainRef from discovery.

name: set_song
description: Change the song's settings: time signature (signatureNumerator, signatureDenominator), swingAmount (0–1, used by the groove and Record Quantization), clipTriggerQuantization (0 none, 1 8 bars, 2 4 bars, 3 2 bars, 4 1 bar, 5 1/2, 6 1/2T, 7 1/4, 8 1/4T, 9 1/8, 10 1/8T, 11 1/16, 12 1/16T, 13 1/32) and midiRecordingQuantization (0 none, 1 1/4, 2 1/8, 3 1/8T, 4 1/8+1/8T, 5 1/16, 6 1/16T, 7 1/16+1/16T, 8 1/32).

name: set_scale
description: Set the Set's scale (Live 12's Scale Mode, which Live's MIDI tools and devices follow): rootNote (0 C … 11 B) and scaleName as Live names it (Major, Minor, Dorian, …); or the loaded tuning's name, lowestNote and highestNote ({indexInOctave, octave}: Live keeps 128 notes between them) and referencePitch ({frequency, indexInOctave, octave}). Live loads a tuning only from its Browser, never from Python, and its note tunings can't be set.

name: set_groove
description: Groove: the global groove amount (action set-amount, grooveAmount 0–1.3), or one groove in the pool (action edit, grooveRef, with base, quantizationAmount, timingAmount, randomAmount, velocityAmount 0–1).

name: replace_sample
description: Swap the sample in a Simpler for another: deviceRef (the Simpler), and sample, the path of an audio file (one find_sounds returned, or any on this computer).

name: import_audio
description: Put an audio file into the Set as a clip: into an empty Session slot (trackRef, an audio track, and sceneIndex) or into an Arrangement take lane (takeLaneRef, position in beats, past the lane's last clip: Live would cut a take the file lands on, and its API can't put one back). sample is the path of an audio file on this computer (one find_sounds returned, a recording, the producer's own).

name: set_warp_markers
description: Add, move or delete a warp marker in an audio clip, by its beat time (move takes distance in beats). Read them first with live_warp_marker_read.

name: capture_midi
description: Capture MIDI: turn what was just played on armed MIDI tracks into a clip (Live's Capture MIDI).

name: set_device_details
description: Settings a device has beyond its parameters (EQ Eight's oversampling and band editing, Drift, Drum Cell, Hybrid Reverb, Meld and plug-in specifics), as the bridge describes them for the device.

name: use_looper
description: Operate or set a Looper device: record, overdub, play, stop, clear, undo, double or halve speed and length, as the bridge offers them.

name: delete_clip
description: Delete a clip, in the Session or the Arrangement (clipRef from discovery). Kumi's undo brings it back (its answer names anything it won't; never per-note expression or follow actions, which Live doesn't give Kumi).

name: delete_scene
description: Delete a Session scene and the clips in its slots (sceneRef from discovery). Kumi can't bring it back (Live's own undo can). Later scenes move up.

name: delete_track
description: Delete an audio, MIDI or group track with its clips and devices (trackRef from discovery; a group takes the tracks in it). Kumi can't bring it back (Live's own undo can). Later tracks move up.

name: delete_locator
description: Delete an Arrangement locator (locatorRef from discovery). Kumi can't bring it back (Live's own undo can).

name: write_arrangement_clip
description: Write a new MIDI clip with its notes straight into the Arrangement: trackRef (a MIDI track from discovery), start and length in beats from the Set's start, notes (pitch, start and duration in beats from the clip's start, velocity), name and looping optional. Or give notation (Kumi's notation, in song time: bars and beats of the Set) instead of notes, and leave start and length out: the clip spans the bars its notes are in. Several at once: clips, a list of those. No recording, no copying from the Session.

name: clear_range
description: Clear a stretch of the Arrangement on one track: the clips inside it go, and clips crossing its edges are cut there (trackRef, fromBeat, toBeat). Kumi's undo puts them back (its answer names anything it won't; never per-note expression or follow actions, which Live doesn't give Kumi).

name: edit_device
description: Edit what a device has beyond its parameters (deviceRef from discovery): a setting of Roar, Shifter, Spectral Resonator, Hybrid Reverb, CC Control or Simpler (action set: setting, value; the preview lists a setting's choices), how much a Wavetable modulation source moves a target (action modulate), Simpler's slices (slice-insert, slice-move, slice-remove at a time; slice-clear, slice-reset), and its sample's warping (warp-as beats, warp-double, warp-half).

name: duplicate_device
description: Copy an effect with its settings, straight after itself in its chain (deviceRef from discovery). Not an instrument: a chain holds one, so for a second one duplicate its track (change_structure duplicate-track).

name: set_sidechain
description: Feed a device from another track: a compressor's (or gate's, or auto filter's) sidechain, with action sidechain, deviceRef and routingType (the source track) exactly as Live names it (discover the device to see its choices); action routing for a device's own audio or MIDI input, which also takes routingChannel. The classic: the kick ducking the bass.

name: group_tracks
description: Group contiguous top-level trackRefs with playback stopped. References from earlier in this answer still name the same tracks afterwards; the answer says when they don't. This has no Kumi HISTORY inverse.

name: set_scene_follow_actions
description: Set scene Follow Actions with playback stopped: ref is a scene; edit contains enabled, linked, action_a/action_b, chance_a/chance_b, jump_a/jump_b, time in beats or loop_count. Chances sum to 100.

name: set_global_follow_actions
description: Enable or disable global Follow Actions with playback stopped: edit contains enabled.

name: set_note_expression
description: Replace one note expression lane with playback stopped: ref is a clip, noteId is a stable note ID, dimension is pitch/slide/pressure. edit contains exists and up to 4096 events [note-relative beats,value,x1,y1,x2,y2]; pitch is cents, slide/pressure MIDI 0–127. Longer existing lanes are refused to preserve restoration.

name: edit_arrangement_automation
description: Edit track-owned Arrangement automation with playback stopped: ref is the track, targetRef a continuous parameter. edit is action insert with event [Song beats,value,0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5], or action delete with start/end in Song beats. Restoration preserves the complete opaque snapshot within the current adapter session.

name: map_modulator
description: Map one of a modulator's slots to a parameter, as its Map button does, with the map_modulation Willington's DeviceTools give Live's modulators. deviceRef is an LFO, Shaper or Envelope Follower (8 slots) or an Expression Control (5, one per source): load_device them from modulators/LFO, modulators/Shaper, modulators/Envelope Follower and modulators/Expression Control, so a plan loads and maps them in one go. slot counts from 0 (0 when left out). The parameter is parameterRef, or targetRef (its device, an @name too) with parameter, its name as the device shows it ("Filter Freq"). clear: true empties the slot. Kumi's undo empties a slot it filled.

deviceRef.description: The modulator: its reference from discovery, or the @name a step gave it

targetRef.description: The device whose parameter it moves

parameter.description: That parameter's name, as the device shows it

parameterRef.description: Or the parameter itself, from discovery

name: play
description: Play, stop and the like: start (from the start marker; set it first with set_transport's position), continue (from where it stopped), stop, play-selection, stop-all-clips, back-to-arrangement (Live's Back to Arrangement button: tracks that followed their Session clips play the Arrangement again), tap-tempo, nudge-up and nudge-down, re-enable-automation, trigger-session-record. Use it whenever hearing or stopping helps: to check or show what you built, or to record.

name: fire_scene
description: Launch a scene (every clip in its row), as clicking its launch button does. ref is the scene from discovery.

name: launch_clip
description: Launch one Session clip to hear it: slotRef is its clip slot, from discovery.

name: record
description: Start or stop recording: action start or stop, lane session or arrangement, and destinationTrackRef, the armed track (arm it with set_routing first). Live records onto every armed track, so Kumi disarms any other first (only this one records) and says which. Recording keeps what it records in the Set; stop it with action stop.

alsoTrackRefs.description: More armed tracks recorded at the same time (bridge 1.0.47): several sources rendered in one pass

name: jump_to_locator
description: Move the playhead to a locator: direction next or previous, or ref for a particular one.

name: select
description: Show the producer something by selecting it in Live: trackRef, sceneRef, slotRef, detailClipRef (opens it in the Clip view) or chainRef. Use it whenever showing something helps: where a thing is, or what you just built. (Live's scripting can't select a device or a parameter reliably: select its track, or its chain, instead.)

name: show
description: Change what Live shows: focus-view with view Session, Arranger, Detail, Detail/Clip, Detail/DeviceChain or Browser; hide-view; zoom-in, zoom-out, scroll-left, scroll-right; follow-on, follow-off; collapse-track or expand-track (trackRef); browser-toggle.

name: make_changes
description: Make changes in one call, in order: each step is one of your change tools (or play, record, fire_scene and the like) with its input, and "@name" in an input stands for what an earlier step marked as: "name" made (a new track, a loaded device). A wait step ({"beats": 8} or {"seconds": 4}) lets a recording run, as in bouncing a sound to audio: route and arm a new audio track, record, play, wait, stop. It stops at the first step that fails and says what was done. With final: true and every step done, Kumi tells the producer what changed and the answer ends there, with no reply from you: use it when the changes complete the request, even a single change. Steps that aren't tools of your own take these inputs (`?`: may be left out; find_tools gives a step's whole input): load_sample: Load a sample into a new Simpler on an empty MIDI track (trackRef, sample); load_sample_to_pad: Load a sample onto an empty pad of a Drum Rack, in a new Simpler on… (deviceRef, note, sample, instrument?); set_chain_mixer: Balance a rack's chains; set_locators: Mark a section in the Arrangement with two named locators; set_track_color: Change a track's colour to one of Live's 70 palette colours; set_transport: Change the transport; set_routing: Route a track and get it ready to record; set_mixer_options: A track's other mixer settings; edit_rack_mapping: Experimental Willington rack edits; set_clip_follow_actions: Set Session clip Follow Actions with experimental Willington support; set_clip: Change a clip's settings; set_audio_clip: Change an audio clip; edit_clip: Edit a clip's content; move_clip: Move a clip; add_arrangement_clip: Put a clip in the Arrangement at position (trackRef, position, length?, takeLaneRef?, sample?, name?); add_take_lane: Add a take lane to a track in the Arrangement (trackRef, name?); change_notes: Change notes already in a clip, Session or Arrangement, by id; delete_notes: Delete notes from a clip, Session or Arrangement, by id; edit_notes: Quantize a clip's notes; transform_midi: Transform or generate a clip's notes; set_scene: Change a scene; capture_scene: Capture the clips playing now into a new scene; switch_device: Switch a device on or off (deviceRef, enabled); move_device: Move a device along its own track's chain (deviceRef, index); move_device_to: Move a device to another track (deviceRef, targetTrackRef?, targetChainRef?, index?); delete_device: Delete a device; set_chain: Change a rack chain; set_song: Change the song's settings; set_scale: Set the Set's scale; set_groove: Groove; replace_sample: Swap the sample in a Simpler for another (deviceRef, sample); import_audio: Put an audio file into the Set as a clip (sample, trackRef?, sceneIndex?, takeLaneRef?, position?, name?); set_warp_markers: Add, move or delete a warp marker in an audio clip, by its beat time; capture_midi: Capture MIDI; set_device_details: Settings a device has beyond its parameters; use_looper: Operate or set a Looper device; delete_clip: Delete a clip, in the Session or the Arrangement; delete_scene: Delete a Session scene and the clips in its slots; delete_track: Delete an audio, MIDI or group track with its clips and devices; delete_locator: Delete an Arrangement locator; write_arrangement_clip: Write a new MIDI clip with its notes straight into the Arrangement; clear_range: Clear a stretch of the Arrangement on one track; edit_device: Edit what a device has beyond its parameters; duplicate_device: Copy an effect with its settings, straight after itself in its chain; set_sidechain: Feed a device from another track; group_tracks: Group contiguous top-level trackRefs with playback stopped (trackRefs); set_scene_follow_actions: Set scene Follow Actions with playback stopped (ref, edit); set_global_follow_actions: Enable or disable global Follow Actions with playback stopped (edit); set_note_expression: Replace one note expression lane with playback stopped (ref, noteId, dimension, edit); edit_arrangement_automation: Edit track-owned Arrangement automation with playback stopped (ref, targetRef, edit); map_modulator: Map one of a modulator's slots to a parameter, as its Map button does,… (deviceRef, slot?, targetRef?, parameter?, parameterRef?, clear?); fire_scene: Launch a scene; launch_clip: Launch one Session clip to hear it (slotRef); record: Start or stop recording (action, lane, destinationTrackRef?, alsoTrackRefs?); jump_to_locator: Move the playhead to a locator; select: Show the producer something by selecting it in Live (trackRef?, sceneRef?, slotRef?, detailClipRef?, chainRef?); show: Change what Live shows.

input.description: What that tool takes; "@name" for what an earlier step made; wait takes {"beats": 8} or {"seconds": 4}

as.description: Name what this step makes (a new track, a loaded device) for later steps

each.description: Repeat this step: each field's list gives that input field its value run by run, e.g. {"note": [36, 37, 38, 39]}, or several lists of one length, e.g. {"parameterRef": ["parameter:3", "parameter:9"], "value": [0.5, 1]}

final.description: These changes complete the request: Kumi says what changed and you aren't called again. Leave it out to see the results and carry on.

name: arrange
description: Lay out an arrangement in the Arrangement from the producer's own clips, in one call: the sections in order, each with its name, its length in bars and the tracks that play in it, from Session scenes (a section plays a scene's clips, or chosen clips per track) or from a loop already in the Arrangement (loop: its bars; its MIDI clips are copied with their notes). Kumi copies the clips (whole loops, and a loop's first part where a section ends sooner), adds the gaps, fills and risers asked for, marks each section with a locator and puts the playhead at the start. It's one change: one line in HISTORY whose undo takes it all back, and one Cmd-Z in Live. Without sections it changes nothing and returns the material to plan with: each scene's clips by track with their lengths, where the Arrangement's clips end, and its locators. Vary it by subtraction and addition: tracks in and out per section; gap: tracks drop out for the last beats before the next section (the breath before a drop); fill: a track's other clip (its fill or a variation) in place of the loop's end; riser: a clip on an effects track (a riser, a sweep, a crash) placed to end where the section ends.

sections.description: The form, in order. Left out, nothing changes and the material comes back

name.description: Its name, for its locator: Intro, Verse, Build, Drop, Break, Outro…

scene.description: The scene whose clips play here (0 is the first); left out, the arrangement's scene

tracks.description: The tracks that play, each with its clip in this section's scene, or {track, scene} for another of its clips; [] is silence. Left out, every track with a clip in the scene

anyOf.description: A track's name, or its ref

track.description: A track's name, or its ref

scene.description: The scene its clip is in (0 is the first)

gap.description: Tracks stop this many beats before the section ends

items.description: A track's name, or its ref

tracks.description: Which; left out, every track that plays

track.description: A track's name, or its ref

scene.description: The scene its clip is in (0 is the first)

fill.description: A track's other clip, played at the section's end in place of the loop's end

track.description: A track's name, or its ref

scene.description: The scene its clip is in (0 is the first)

riser.description: A clip on a track that doesn't play here (an effects track), placed to end where the section ends

scene.description: The scene a section plays when it names none; left out, the first scene with clips

loop.description: Arrange from bars already in the Arrangement instead: a section's tracks then play what they have there, unless they name a scene

start_bar.description: Where the arrangement starts; left out, after the clips already in the Arrangement

final.description: The arrangement completes the request: Kumi says what it built and you aren't called again

name: undo_change
description: Undo one of your changes from this session: pass its change id (such as c3), or "last" for the latest one. It only works while nobody changed the same thing in Live since; if so, say what happened. With final: true, when the undo is all that was asked, Kumi tells the producer and the answer ends there, with no reply from you.

change.description: A change id such as c3, or "last"

final.description: true when the undo completes the request: Kumi tells the producer, and the answer ends there

name: watch_me
description: Learn a routine the producer does by hand in Live: action start just before they do it (Kumi notes the Set as it is; nothing in Live changes), then action stop when they say they're done. Stop gives what changed: tracks added (with routing, arming, monitoring), devices loaded (with the knobs they turned from Live's defaults; switches and modes aren't compared), clips recorded or made, and settings changed, each with its track. Save it at once with save_recipe as the steps that would redo it, with $blanks for what differs each time (the source track, say), leaving out anything clearly unrelated: a device as load_device (as: "sat") and each knob turned as set_device_parameter with deviceRef "@sat" and the knob's name as parameter. Then say in a few words what the recipe does. The producer can ask you to change it.

name: audition
description: Hear what you built and how close it is to a reference, in one call: Kumi plays the part and hears each candidate track after its devices, compares it with the reference, then puts everything back. The producer hears the first candidate in the Set, and Kumi hears the others on their own, so put the one you lean toward first. Up to 8 candidates are heard together in one real-time pass, so try several ideas at once (different instruments, chains, settings on separate tracks). Say where the part is: from_beat and beats in the Arrangement, or a Session clip per candidate (clip), which Kumi plays from the Arrangement for the render and removes after. A candidate can be the whole mix ({"mix": true}, on its own): what Main plays at from_beat, heard like a track; audition it against a reference to match a mix, changing EQ, compression and levels between rounds. Returns each candidate's closeness to the reference (0–100) with the biggest gaps in words, and what it heard. A silent render is reported, not compared. Without a reference it only listens.

candidates.description: The tracks to render, each on its own (a candidate sound, or the track to check), or the whole mix

mix.description: true: the whole mix (Main's output) instead of a track

clip.description: A Session clip on that track to play (its clipRef); left out, the Arrangement at from_beat

label.description: A short name for it ("Collision + parallel delay")

from_beat.description: Where the part starts in the Arrangement, in beats (a 4/4 bar is 4)

beats.description: How long to render, in beats; a clip's length when left out, 8 at most by default

reference.description: What to match: an audio file's path or ~/…, or an audio clip's clipRef

reference_from_seconds.description: Where in the reference the part is

reference_seconds.description: How much of the reference to hear

focus.description: sound: one patch or hit (timbre, envelope, pitch); section: a part or mix (balance, density, rhythm too). Left out, by length

name: judge
description: Work toward a sound goal in rounds, as an engineer would: Kumi listens, finds the biggest gap, you make one change, and Kumi keeps it only if the evidence says so. Start a run with goal: what to reach (loudness in LUFS, a true_peak ceiling in dBTP), a reference (an audio file or clip whose tonal balance, dynamics and low end become targets, each with its range, and for a mix its loudness, at its median ±0.5 LU), focus (a track that must cut through: masking is measured against it) and explicit targets. Kumi hears the mix (or track) once, as the producer does, and answers with the checklist: each item's value, what it wants and how many just-noticeable steps it's off, the problems it found placed in time and frequency (harsh hits at 0:42, 5.8–7.2 kHz, +9 dB over the local level; a steady resonance; stereo lows; one bass note louder than the rest; the vocal buried 1–4 kHz), and the next target with the kind of fix it calls for. Make ONE change toward that target with Live's devices, then call judge again with change saying what you did. Kumi hears the same bars again, brings the level back where it belongs (the goal's loudness, or where it was) with the last Live Limiter on the track, else a Utility it adds, compares every item there, keeps the change only if its target improved and nothing else got audibly worse (it takes the change back itself otherwise: don't undo it yourself), and names the next target. Let the problem pick the tool: a steady imbalance is a static EQ (EQ Eight), one that comes and goes is a dynamic band (Multiband Dynamics) or a de-esser, peaks are a limiter, wide lows are mono below a frequency (Utility's Bass Mono), a buried element is a dip in the others keyed from it. Fix a problem where it starts when you can (the hi-hats' harshness on the hi-hat track, not the master). When a target resists two changes in a row, Kumi moves on to the next and comes back to it later. Keep going until every item is within tolerance or changes stop helping (in a /loop, Kumi decides that and asks you), then call judge with done: true, which hears the whole stretch again and reports before → after.

goal.description: Starts a run (and ends any other; inside a /loop, a second goal is refused)

reference.description: A reference: one measured with the reference tool (its name), an audio file's path (~/…) or an audio clip's clipRef

problems.description: Clear what Kumi's detectors find (true when left out)

sound.description: A single sound (a patch, a hit) against a reference sound: its attack, decay, where it settles, brightness, noisiness, pitch drop (an 808's or a kick's), modulation rate, width, top (bandwidth), noise floor, warmth (2nd and 3rd harmonics), tail and crackle join the checklist, and its effects: a reverb's decay time and how its tail darkens, echoes' time and fall, how deep it swings, how far its brightness sweeps and its tail's share. Judge it on the track that plays it (track)

focus.description: The track that must cut through the rest (its ref or name)

measure.description: dynamics: peak to loudness (dB); density: peak to short-term loudness (dB); range: loudness range (LU); punch: crest (dB); pumping: how far the mids' level swings at 0.5–6 Hz (dB); distortion: how much brighter the loudest moments are than middling ones (dB); low_width: side under mid below 120 Hz (dB); rumble: under 30 Hz against 30–120 Hz (dB); brightness: the spectrum's tilt (dB per octave, 0 is pink; not a sound's brightness in Hz, which comes from a reference sound); decay_time: a reverb's RT60 (s); tail_darkening: how much its tails darken (octaves); echo_time: ms between echoes; echo_fall: dB each echo falls; swing: modulation depth (dB); sweep: how far its brightness moves (octaves); tail_share: its tail's share of its energy (%)

track.description: With goal: judge one track (its ref or name) instead of the mix

from_beat.description: With goal: where the stretch starts in the Arrangement, in beats (the whole song when left out)

beats.description: With goal: how long the stretch is, in beats

change.description: What you changed since the last judge call, in one line

done.description: End the run: hear the whole stretch again and report before → after

name: tune
description: Code picks the numbers for a change you chose, against the judged run's checklist, and Kumi judges the result as a round (kept or taken back, like judge with change). Put the device where the fix belongs first (make_changes), then tune it. how: "fit" calculates an EQ Eight's bands from what was measured, with no trial listens: the smallest cut that clears a steady resonance or harshness, or bands that close the balance gaps toward the reference while holding the regions already in tolerance (it uses the EQ's free bands, and turns Adaptive Q off and Scale to 100% so they land as calculated). "home" moves one knob where more means more until its target is met, each probe heard on the target's excerpt: a limiter's gain toward a loudness, its ceiling toward a true peak, a de-esser's or dynamic band's threshold until the harsh hits drop, an EQ band's gain until the vocal stops being masked. "search" tunes 2–5 knobs that interact (a compressor's attack, release and ratio; a reverb's size, decay and damping) on the run's own track (judge with track; a plain track, not a group): small generations of candidates, each generation heard side by side on scratch copies of the track in one pass, and kept only if one beats where the knobs are. "probe" hears one knob across its range in one pass (seven settings, on scratch copies of the run's own track), saves what it does to each measure, then sets it where its response meets the target (never past a setting that made something else worse) and judges that: one pass and one judged listen, and the right way to a number read off a reference, like a reverb's decay time or a delay's echo time. Homing a knob toward a measure it was probed or homed on before starts where its saved response says. The copies play without the focus track, so masking is homed in on, not searched or probed. Prefer tune over guessing numbers yourself: it takes fewer listens.

device.description: The device's ref (from discovery or make_changes)

target.description: The checklist item it's for (its id, such as "loudness" or "resonance 1.1 khz"); the run's next target when left out

knobs.description: The knobs’ names as the device shows them, or roles: a mapped plug-in's (the plug-in guide lists them, such as "ceiling" on Ozone 12) or a job any device does ("limiter gain", "ceiling", "eq gain": on EQ Eight, the nearest band that's on (a bell or a shelf for a gain), within about an octave of the target's frequency; otherwise Kumi asks which). One for home or probe (such as "Gain" or "Decay Time"), 2–5 for search

change.description: What the change is, in a few words, for the log

name: groove
description: Shape a part's feel toward a reference's, judged on the notes with no listening: where each lane plays (a part on a Drum Rack in lanes by its pads: kick, snare, hats, cymbals and perc; any other part one lane), its timing step by step (push, swing, laid-back hats), its velocity accents, syncopation and fills (with 8 bars or more). Start a run with clip (the part, a MIDI clip) and reference (a MIDI clip with the reference's notes). For a reference's drums: put the track in the Arrangement, separate its stems (live_command separate_stems), convert the drum stem to MIDI (live_command convert_drums_to_midi), and give that MIDI clip as reference and the drum stem's clip as audio: Kumi hears the stem and moves each converted hit onto its real onset. For a pitched part that isn't in Live (a bass line in an audio file), give the file as reference: Kumi turns its first 2 minutes into notes with Basic Pitch, on a grid fitted to them (its tempo near reference_tempo or the estimate, and its first downbeat; the reply says it), and its velocities aren't compared: its timing and swing are, not its accents. Then change the notes (change_notes, transform_midi swing, quantize) and call groove with change, or let code move the notes toward the reference's timing and accents with apply: true (amount 0–1, all the way when left out). Kumi keeps a change only if its target got closer and nothing else moved away, taking it back otherwise, and names the next target. done: true ends the run with before → after.

clip.description: Starts a run: the part, a MIDI clip's clipRef

reference.description: Starts a run: the reference's MIDI clip (its clipRef), or an audio file of a pitched part that isn't in Live (Basic Pitch turns it into notes, on a grid fitted to them)

reference_tempo.description: With an audio file as the reference: its tempo, BPM: its grid is fitted within 2 % of it (Kumi estimates it when left out, trying half and double too)

audio.description: The reference's drum stem (an Arrangement audio clip's clipRef): its hits' onsets refine the reference's timing

change.description: What you changed in the part, to judge it

apply.description: Code moves the part's notes toward the reference's timing and accents, then judges that

amount.description: With apply: how far (1, all the way, when left out)

done.description: Ends the run: before → after on every line

name: form
description: Lay out the song's form, heard. Kumi plays the whole Arrangement (or from_beat for beats), listening as it plays, and reads it bar by bar: the energy curve (loudness, density, brightness, low end); the sections it falls into (their bars, role: intro, build, peak, break, verse or outro, and a letter shared by sections that sound alike); the turns between them (a drop or a fall, and what prepares it: a build, a gap or a riser); the intro and outro lengths and the bar the first hook starts on; which tracks play where, from the Arrangement's clips; and the problems a form can have: neighbouring sections without contrast, energy that plateaus, odd phrase lengths, a drop that arrives unprepared, a stretch left unchanged for 32 bars and more. With a reference (an audio file or a clip in the Set), its form too, read in its own bars (its tempo and first downbeat fitted to its onsets, half or double when that's nearer this Set's tempo; this Set's bars when its tempo can't be told), and how the two differ. A whole-song listen takes as long as the song.

from_beat.description: Where to start, in beats (the Arrangement's start when left out)

beats.description: How long, in beats (to the song's last clip when left out)

reference.description: A song to compare the form with: an audio file or a clip in the Set (its clipRef)

name: sound
description: Measure sounds in Live: the tracks heard side by side in one pass (8 bars from from_beat unless beats says). Each sound gets its attack, decay (and how it sits against a beat), sustain, brightness, noisiness, pitch drop (an 808's or a kick's), modulation rate (and the beats a cycle), warmth (2nd and 3rd harmonics, even against odd), width, top (bandwidth), noise floor, tail (a dry hit falls far, a reverberant one hangs on) and crackle, and its effects: its decay time (RT60, said as a reverb when its tails fall in two slopes, the second slower) and how its tails darken and widen, echoes (their time as a note value, repeats, how far each falls and darkens), how deep its level swings, how far its brightness moves (a filter sweeping; a bass line's read against its notes) and how often, pumping against the beat, and its tail's share bar by bar. Plus its problems: clicks at note edges, DC, a note jumping out, tails cut off, echoes out of time, repeats that don't die away, an effect's tail burying the dry hits. Several tracks are judged as a kit too: a piece whose noise floor, top or grit sits apart from pieces of a similar range, pieces piling up or a wide gap between them, a piece ringing into its own next hit, and pieces that sound the same. With against (a kick, say), how far each track ducks under it and how fast it comes back, and whether their hits interlock or collide. With key, how far a low part's notes (its bass line) sit from it. To move a sound toward a reference sound, judge it with goal.sound.

tracks.description: The tracks to measure (names or refs)

against.description: A track the others duck under or play against (its name or ref)

key.description: The song's key, like "F# minor", "Bb major" or "D dorian"

from_beat.description: Where to listen from, in beats

beats.description: How long, in beats (8 bars when left out)

name: render
description: Render an audio track's own clips (its recordings, a bounce) between two points to a file at once: offline and silent, no transport, no recording. It's the raw audio, before the track's devices; instruments, effects and the mix aren't in it (for those, audition, or record by resampling). Returns the file for listen, to hear it or compare it with a reference.

track.description: An audio track (its reference from this turn)

from_beat.description: Where to start in the Arrangement, in beats (a 4/4 bar is 4)

name: undo_in_live
description: Live's own undo (or redo, with redo: true), once, exactly like Cmd-Z in Live: for something the producer did in Live themselves, or a change of Kumi's that undo_change can't take back (a crop, or a change undo_change says it can't). For Kumi's other changes use undo_change, which undoes exactly that change; this undoes whatever Live did last.

name: run_python
description: Run Python inside Live for anything your typed tools don't cover; use those first. Explore Live's API with dir(). mode eval returns an expression; exec (default) returns whatever you assign to result. Names: Live, song, app, obj (optional ref), bridge. Returns JSON {ok, result, stdout, error}, with Live objects as usable {ref, type, name} and errors as type, message and traceback. Each run opens one step in Live's undo or joins an already open step; undo_in_live takes it back. No HISTORY entry or undo_change. Set reads and old references are discarded after every run, including failures. timeoutMs defaults to 5000 (1–30000), checked by Python tracing; native calls finish before the deadline can be checked.

name: live_command
description: Use Live's own commands, through its menus and keys, for what your other tools can't do: group or ungroup tracks, freeze, unfreeze or flatten a track, bounce a track or clip to audio without playing it (bounce_to_new_track, bounce_track_in_place), consolidate, convert an audio clip to MIDI (melody, harmony, drums), separate stems, slice to a MIDI track, save the Set (or collect all and save), save it as a new file (save_as with path), start a new Set (new_set) or open one (open_set with path), export audio or a MIDI clip. new_set and open_set replace the open Set: say what happens to its unsaved changes with save_current (ask the producer when they didn't say), and references from before are gone once it's open: its answer then has the Set as it is (now), with current references, so carry on in it. Give final: true to the command that finishes the request (a save, a save as, the new Set) and Kumi tells the producer itself. Kumi fills Live's Save and Open dialogs on Windows only: on a Mac, ask the producer to save as or open a Set in Live. When a file is already at path, Live asks before replacing it: ask the producer, never answer it yourself. Live keeps a Set in a project folder: saved as into a folder that isn't one, it makes "<name> Project" there, and the result says where the Set went. Never make or edit .als files yourself: Live calls a Set it didn't write corrupt. Give the command and what it works on (track, tracks side by side, or clip): Kumi selects it in Live, presses the command, and says what changed. separate_stems takes stems (vocals, drums, bass, others; all four when left out), quality (high quality or high speed; as the producer last left it when left out) and merge (true puts two or three stems on one track): Kumi fills Live's Separate Stems dialog, presses Separate, waits while Live works (a minute or more for a whole song) and says the new tracks. For anything else Live's menus or keys do, give menu (the item's titles, ["Create", "Insert Silence"]) or keys (["cmd+e"]). When Live opens a dialog, its words, buttons and toggles (check boxes, on or off) come back: toggles sets them by name and answer presses a button, both in one call. Given with a command, toggles and answer go to the dialog it opens. Live comes to the front for a moment. Prefer your other tools whenever one does the job.

command.description: One of Live's commands Kumi knows

track.description: The track it works on (its reference from this turn, or its name)

tracks.description: Tracks side by side (to group them), first to last

clip.description: The clip it works on: its clipRef from this turn (a Session clip; for converting to MIDI, an audio clip in Session or Arrangement), or "selected" for the one the producer selected in Live

stems.description: For separate_stems: the stems to make (all four when left out)

quality.description: For separate_stems: Live's quality mode (as the producer last left it when left out)

merge.description: For separate_stems with two or three stems: true puts them together on one track

path.description: The Set's file, a full path (Windows): where save_as saves it (its folder must exist; .als is added), which Set open_set opens, or where save puts a Set never saved

save_current.description: For new_set and open_set when the open Set has unsaved changes: yes saves them first, no discards them, cancel keeps the Set open

final.description: true when this command finishes the request (the save, the save as, the new or opened Set): Kumi tells the producer what it did, and you aren't called again

menu.description: Any of Live's menu items by its titles, ["Edit", "Freeze Track"]

keys.description: Keys to press in Live, one combination each: "cmd+shift+r", "down"

toggles.description: Set toggles of the dialog Live has open by name, true on and false off, before answer presses its button: {"Vocals": true, "Drums": false}

answer.description: Press this button of the dialog Live has open (OK, Export, Cancel…)

name: plugin
description: Work with a plug-in (Serum 2, Vital, Ozone, Pro-Q 4, Saturn 2, OTT, Supermassive, Decapitator, Pigments, Pro-L 2, or any other) the way its owner would. Read its guide before working on one. guide: what Kumi knows of it (its architecture, sound-design moves, what isn't a knob and how to get there), matched to its real parameter names, which of them Kumi can turn now (set those with set_device_parameter by name, in the plug-in's own units: "800 Hz", "-6 dB"), and how to get to the rest. wavetable: make a wavetable (keyframes of harmonics or shapes morphing frame to frame, or single cycles cut from a held note) into the plug-in's own wavetable folder, for its oscillator's menu.

device.description: The plug-in device (its deviceRef from this turn)

name.description: What to call it, as it shows in the synth's menu

keyframes.description: Frames it morphs through, first to last

count.description: Frames in all (morphing between keyframes); 64 for a sound cut from audio

from_audio.description: Cut single cycles from a held note instead

name: variations
description: Variations in Live: numbered takes V1, V2… of a source, each its own object, never written over the source. make: source is a Session MIDI clip (clipRef): what it plays, its loop; anchors are the clip's notes every take keeps as they are (their index, from 0, as read_notes' json lists them). Each of takes is a recipe: ops (pitch (semitones, up or down: the notes move), velocity (velocities moved), timing (loosened, in beats), thin (fewer notes); amount 0 to 1), lines (a MIDI clip's notes ({pitch, start, duration, velocity}: beats from the start of what the clip plays; its anchor notes stay as they are: no need to write them)), and/or from: "V2" to start from another take; direction names it in a few words. count without takes picks distinct directions. place: clips (each take in an empty Session slot below the source on its track, a scene added when none is free). options: none in Live. Kumi draws each take and checks it differs from the source and the other takes yet keeps the anchors, the idea, the key and the grid (re-rolling up to 8 times; novelty subtle, clear or bold, or minDistance 0 to 1; lines you write that come close are written with a warning), writes each as one change, doesn't render them (Live plays a MIDI clip only live: the producer launches the takes' slots to hear them), and answers a line per take. A make on the same source goes on numbering (V10 after V9); another source starts another set, still there by its number or name (set). change: names ("V6", or "rest": every take not kept) and takes (a recipe each, in order; left out, Kumi picks distinct directions) rewrite only those takes, two changes each (Live adds no notes to a clip: its clip is deleted and written again in its slot): kept takes and the source are never touched (force: true only when the producer named a kept take), and a take the producer edited is left as it is. keep: names; each kept take is renamed “V3 · … · kept” in Live (a change each), so the mark is there after a restart too; at places one take: none in Live: a kept take stays in its slot (drag it where it goes). drop: names ("rest" by default) go a change each (one clip each). list: the set's takes. Live's Session clips; notes in beats from the start of what the clip plays

set.description: Which set of takes: its number, or its source's name (the latest by default)

anchors.description: the clip's notes every take keeps as they are (their index, from 0, as read_notes' json lists them)

from.description: Another take to start from, such as V2

lines.description: a MIDI clip's notes ({pitch, start, duration, velocity}: beats from the start of what the clip plays; its anchor notes stay as they are: no need to write them)

minDistance.description: How far each take must be from the source and the others (instead of novelty)

listen.description: false skips rendering the takes to hear them (on by default)
